An attacker on the native VLAN sends frames crafted so the access switch strips one 802.1Q tag and forwards them, still tagged, into a VLAN the attacker cannot normally reach. Which attack is this?
fixes.e: Double tagging abuses native-VLAN handling: the outer tag is stripped and the switch forwards the still-tagged frame into the victim VLAN. Switch spoofing is the other VLAN-hopping variant, but it works by negotiating a trunk over DTP rather than by nesting tags.

fixes.e: Co-channel interference occurs when access points share one channel and their clients must defer to each other, cutting usable airtime and throughput. Adjacent-channel interference comes from overlapping but different channels and shows up as noise rather than orderly contention; spacing neighboring APs across non-overlapping channels such as 1, 6, and 11 in 2.4 GHz avoids both.

fixes.x: A switch in a cramped, unventilated wiring closet spontaneously reboots most afternoons in July. Which is the MOST likely cause?
fixes.e: Heat in an enclosed closet peaks in the afternoon, and network gear thermal-protects itself by shutting down or resetting. A memory leak tracks uptime rather than time of day, PoE exhaustion drops powered ports instead of restarting the switch, and lighting interference corrupts frames, not power. Add airflow or AC and keep fans and vents clear.
